cards.explanation: The answer is True. The angel says, “The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent His angel to show His servants what must soon take place.” So the One behind this whole vision is the Lord Himself. And look who it's for, friends: His servants.

The answer is whoever keeps the words of this book. Verse 7 says, “Blessed is the one who keeps the words of prophecy in this book.” Keeping is the word, friends, not just glancing at it once. I've glanced at a recipe card and set it down before, and the cookies never came out right.

The answer is worship. Verse 8 says John “…fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown me these things.” That's a big move, and I think John was completely overwhelmed. The next verse is where the angel sets him straight.

The answer is servant. The angel says, “I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book.” Notice that word fellow, friends. He's standing right alongside John, not above him.

The answer is God. The angel says it in just two words: “Worship God!” John had the right idea of worshiping, just the wrong direction. The angel points him straight up to the One who deserves it. A good messenger sends the attention to the One who sent him.

The answer is False. The angel says, “Do not seal up the words of prophecy in this book, because the time is near.” A sealed cookie box keeps the cookies safe, but this book is not meant to be shut up. Near is the word, friends.

The answer is True. The angel says, “let the righteous continue to practice righteousness, and the holy continue to be holy.” The verse has two sides, and this is the second half. It's a heavy verse, friends, but it doesn't stop on the heavy part.
The answer is by what each one has done. The verse says, “…My reward is with Me, to give to each one according to what he has done.” Each one, friends, not just a few. That's how it is measured.

The answer is the tree of life. Verse 14 says those who wash their robes get “…the right to the tree of life…” It's a blessing, and the verse names it straight out. The tree of life is also named in the next warning in verse 19.
The answer is True. Verse 14 says they “…may enter the city by its gates.” So it's two gifts in one blessing, friends: the tree of life and the city. Washed robes, open gates.

The answer is False. Verse 15 puts them outside: “But outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.” That's a heavy verse, and I won't make light of it. It sits right after the blessing for those who enter by the gates.
The answer is David, Israel's king. Jesus says, “I am the Root and the Offspring of David…” That ties Him to David's own family line. Two titles, one name, friends.

The answer is the one who hears. The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” and then comes the open invitation: “Let the one who hears say, ‘Come!’” That could be anyone who hears it, friends. Including you. The invitation is out there, and the ones who hear it get to pass it on.

The answer is water. The verse says, “…let the one who is thirsty come, and the one who desires the water of life drink freely.” Thirsty and water go together, friends. And notice that word freely. It's right there in the verse.

The answer is plagues. Verse 18 says, “If anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues described in this book.” It's a serious warning, friends, and I'll leave it as serious. Those are the words, just as they stand.

The answer is True. Verse 19 says, “…God will take away his share in the tree of life and the holy city, which are described in this book.” It's the other half of the warning in verse 18. Serious on both ends, friends.
The answer is to come. The plea is, “Come, Lord Jesus!” It answers the promise right before it, “Yes, I am coming soon.” That's the whole prayer, friends, and it's short.
The answer is False, and I'm glad. The last verse says, “The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all the saints. Amen.” It isn't for John alone. All the saints is a much bigger table, friends.
